title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA GRACES THE VALEDICTORY CEREMONY OF THE GOLDEN JUBILEE CELEBRATIONS OF THE VAIDYARATNAM AYURVEDA COLLEGE
subtitle: AYURVEDIC COLLEGES SHOULD SERVE THE COMMUNITY WITH AUTHENTIC AND EFFECTIVE AYURVEDA: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
body_text: The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu graced the valedictory ceremony of the Golden Jubilee celebrations of the Vaidyaratnam Ayurveda College at Thrissur, Keralam today (November 27, 2026). Speaking on the occasion, the President said that Keralam’s contribution goes beyond enhancing the international reputation of Ayurveda. It has nurtured a rich and living tradition of classical Ayurvedic learning. It has also enriched the medical knowledge passed down through generations of Vaidya families. Its traditions of preparing authentic Ayurvedic medicines have continued to flourish unabated. The President said that a remarkable feature of Ayurveda is that its authentic literature has never been limited to Sanskrit. In Keralam, a lot of original work and commentaries have been produced in Malayalam and Manipravalam also. The President said that every Ayurvedic College should serve the community with authentic and effective Ayurveda. It should also impart topical Ayurvedic education. Such colleges should be able to create experts who have the wisdom to effectively respond to the health challenges of the present and future generations. She was happy to note that the work ethos of Vaidyaratnam Ayurveda College is aligned with this dictum. The President said that Ayurvedic institutions like Vaidyaratnam Ayurveda College are making their contribution to achieving the goal of a healthy and Viksit Bharat by 2047. The President w as happy to note a distinctive feature of the Ayurvedic tradition in Keralam which combines Ayurvedic professional practices with philanthropy. She advised students they should demonstrate how the traditional knowledge-based enterprise and service to the less privileged can be dovetailed, when they enter the professional phase of their life.
